look_here_first: Confirm BULB-origin basal trifoliolate leaves and separate LEAFLESS flowering scapes. Examine the small, relatively shallow-notched leaflets (usually 8–15 mm, notch ~1/4–1/3 depth): OXALATE LINES along the notch margins help distinguish O. violacea from O. drummondii. Flower color is not a reliable separator.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Source-pool approved accepted Oxalis violacea concept; no independently verified BONAP/NAPA three-target-county native evidence in this curation pass.

morphology_keys.habit: Stemless bulbous perennial, basal leaves and separate leafless scapes.
morphology_keys.leaves: Basal trifoliolate leaves; 3 obcordate leaflets commonly (5–)8–15(–20) mm, notch ~1/4–1/3 length; oxalate deposits/lines often evident along notch margins.
morphology_keys.flowers: Five petals, often pink to violet; flowering stems are leafless scapes, not leafy aerial stems. Inspect sepals and inflorescence, not just color.
morphology_keys.fruit: Capsules produced on scapes; check mature fruit and bulb for positive ID.

comparisons.key_distinctions: O. drummondii often has larger (6–)14–34 mm leaflets with deeper notch to 4/5 length and no oxalate lines along notch; the two overlap in size. Yellow caulescent woodsorrels have leafy aerial stems, not a bulb with basal leaves and separate scapes.
comparisons.cautions: Notch depth and leaflet width vary; matched-scale macro and bulb origin are needed. Do not diagnose from violet petals or claim project native PASS.
